ambiguities.readings: Page clutter can be recorded as the §5.3 template row (广告、页面上和本文无关的内容) or as 'not a statement'; the standard has no notion of non-statements, so the two labels mean the same and need one name.

A related-story teaser that is a named engineer's estimate of the liquid-cooling market: unrelated page content (not kept), or a kind-3 named estimate about NVIDIA's supplier industry that the override rule forces to keep.

The standard is silent on headlines: a headline can be page furniture (not kept), or the same item as the body statement it summarises (§5.6, kept once); S26 also carries the only sampled statement of the 2028 delay.

ambiguities.sections: §5.1 rule, §5.3 'only these are not kept', §4.3 governance row, §6.2
ambiguities.readings: An immaterial own lease and a routine director indemnification fit no §5.3 row, so the closed list keeps them, while the §5.1 rule (an analyst would note it) drops them; §4.3 says governance items become 'evidence or not kept' but §5.3 has no row for 'not kept'. Their weight is also undefined: optional is defined only as market expectations or pricing, supporting requires bearing on a key judgement.

ambiguities.sections: §5.3 row 2 and its boundary, §6.2 optional, §10 B10
ambiguities.readings: Share prices, market value and multiples are 'not kept' in §5.3 yet 'optional' in §6.2 and §10 B10; keep=false and keep=true/optional are both defensible and score the same, but the single keep field cannot say which the standard means.

The override says anything touching a §5.1 kind is not on a reject row; any company product decision (end driver support for old GPUs, choose a host CPU, name a next CPU) is a kind-1 decision, so row 1 (product parameters) either never applies to the company's own products or applies to product decisions without business scale.

A conditional valuation of Micron: row 3 needs the other company to be unrelated to all of NVIDIA's markets, but Micron is a supplier; row 4's boundary keeps conditional valuations with a derivation without saying whose company; so reject (another company's valuation) or keep as supporting (conditional valuation).
'Analysts cited by Bloomberg' may or may not be a named party; the sentence is either a kind-3 analyst claim on product progress (keep, supporting) or a generic 'could hurt' risk (row 4, not kept).
A scrapped four-die configuration is a product parameter (row 1, not kept) or a change to key product progress (kept).

Row 4 rejects only unargued conclusions; an argued author interpretation (subscription revenue immaterial, licence was friction) is either journalist framing (row 5) or, being off the closed list, a kept kind-3 claim.

Generic explanations in the company's own blog fit no row except 'journalist background', whose name assumes a journalist; either row 5 stretches to any author, or the closed list forces keeping them.
Promotional executive quotes describing benefits fit both 'strategic statement without number or decision' and 'adjective-only quote'; same outcome, different row.

A government probe of DeepSeek's chip use is background in the Singapore-case article: part of the optional Singapore case overview, a kind-4 regulatory step (supporting), or a restatement of a known fact (optional, though extraction cannot know it is old).

Pending item 3 makes the company's own ecosystem numbers optional; a partner's download count that touches none of the seven drivers is either optional by analogy or kept as kind 2 with a weight the standard does not define.

Core needs an amount or definite state AND a time; statements in the present or near future with no explicit date (China will allow, has started guarantees, aims to raise, in talks, over 90% share) are either supporting (time missing) or core (time implicitly now).
A memory supplier's revenue and margin with amount and period touch key input price (step 2: core) but are another company's numbers (step 3: supporting); the steps do not say which wins.
A $3.4 billion purchase commitment announced by the counterparty is like Sharon's contract (another company's contract, supporting) or like the lease guarantee (NVIDIA's own obligation, core).

One item mixes tiers (a completed launch or result with a plan or a company claim; a company plan with a rumoured size); §5.6 makes it one item but §5.5 gives one tier, and the standard does not say whether the item takes the weaker or the main tier.

A company announcing its own completed action or published count is a fact ('official action, published number') or a party statement ('a party's statement about itself'); for B06, Micron is a party to the memory market but a third party to NVIDIA.
A media or research site relaying the company's own production and shipping plan is a third-party view (who reported) or a party statement (original speaker, §5.4).

Valuations fit none of the seven drivers (driver none, yet kept as supporting); a company's own headline guidance (bank net interest income) is the answer itself, not a path, so its driver is either none or a stretched input-cost reading.
Weight is relative to 'some question': for a policy-rate theme question the hike is core; for the bank's own question it is a general driver (supporting).
Granting token credits for a revenue share is pricing and installed base (how customers pay) or capital and obligations (financing customers).

ambiguities.sections: §3.2 other company's quantity, §4.3 customer purchase row, §4.4 component rule
ambiguities.readings: Alphabet's capex is an uncovered company's quantity (§3.2, evidence), a customer's purchase plan (§4.3), or a component with its own drivers of the five-hyperscaler total that §4.4 would open as another question if it passed independent significance.

Total revenue vs data-center revenue is 'a different quantity' (test 4: another question) or 'the same total in another scope' (same question); and whether total revenue counts as the A 'value-carrying' quantity when the A examples name the segment.

§3.2 requires the theme to be on the coverage list only for a pure macro article; for policy or macro themes the standard does not say whether test 1 is judged against the covered universe or against anyone, so the lidar bill could open as an E theme and the Fed rate could need a coverage-list check.

The standard's D text includes input prices, but pending item 2 says that definition is not yet signed and the code uses the narrower industry total; under the narrow definition a DRAM price question would not open.

A regulator's approval of one company's drug fits B (main product node: can the drug launch) and E (policy stage deciding one company's product, asset); opens_as differs (main_driver vs policy_stage).

The rule that an uncovered company's quantity is evidence sits in §3.2, not in the §4.3 closed list or the four tests, so a 'not open' answer must cite a test (settleability) or a section outside the list.
A single lease guarantee may be a separate deal (its own question) or part of the backstop or commitment total already asked as an amount (the same total in another scope).
